name: Demo dataset — General Dentistry (sample data, not for production use)
sourceNote: SAMPLE DATA FOR DEVELOPMENT ONLY. Code numbers are short factual identifiers. All descriptive text in this file was written independently for this application and is NOT the official CDT descriptor set. No official descriptor text is included: the officialDescriptor field is absent from every entry and is populated only by a licensed import. CDT is maintained by the American Dental Association; using official CDT content commercially requires a license from the ADA.

codes.plainLanguage: The routine re-examination of a patient already of record, typically done at a recall visit.
codes.commonUse: Used at recall visits for a patient the practice has seen before and whose history is on file.
codes.distinctions: Differs from a comprehensive evaluation, which is for a new patient or a patient being re-established after a long gap. Differs from a limited evaluation, which addresses a specific problem.
documentationConsiderations: Whether the patient is of record
verifyQuestions: Has this patient been examined by this practice before?
Was this a routine recall visit rather than a specific complaint?

relationships.note: Comprehensive evaluation is for a new patient or re-established patient rather than a routine recall.
A limited evaluation addresses a specific problem rather than a periodic review.

codes.plainLanguage: An examination directed at a specific problem or complaint rather than a general review of the mouth.
codes.commonUse: Used for emergency or problem visits, such as a patient presenting with pain or a fractured tooth.
codes.distinctions: Distinguished by scope: it addresses the presenting problem, not the whole dentition. It is not the routine recall examination.
documentationConsiderations: The specific problem or complaint that prompted the visit
verifyQuestions: Was this visit prompted by a specific complaint or problem?
Was the examination limited to that problem rather than a full review?

relationships.note: A periodic evaluation is the routine recall review rather than a problem-focused visit.

codes.shortLabel: Comprehensive oral evaluation — new or established patient
codes.plainLanguage: A thorough evaluation and recording of the whole mouth, including hard and soft tissues.
codes.commonUse: Used for a new patient, or for an existing patient being re-evaluated after a significant absence or change in health status.
codes.distinctions: Broader than a periodic evaluation. Where a practice uses it for a returning patient, the reason for a comprehensive rather than periodic review matters.
documentationConsiderations: Whether the patient is new to the practice
verifyQuestions: Is this a new patient, or an established patient being comprehensively re-evaluated?
What prompted a comprehensive rather than periodic evaluation?

relationships.note: Periodic evaluation is the routine recall review for a patient of record.

codes.shortLabel: Intraoral complete series of radiographic images
codes.plainLanguage: A complete intraoral radiographic survey of the dentition and surrounding structures.
codes.commonUse: Used at a comprehensive examination, typically at intervals set by the practice's radiographic protocol.
codes.distinctions: A complete series is a defined set of images. Taking several periapicals and bitewings at one visit is not automatically a complete series.
documentationConsiderations: Number and type of images captured
Date of the previous complete series
Clinical reason the series was indicated
verifyQuestions: How many images were taken, and of what type?
Does this meet your protocol's definition of a complete series?

relationships.note: A panoramic image is a single extraoral image, not an intraoral series.

codes.plainLanguage: The first periapical image taken at a visit. A periapical shows the whole tooth including the root tip and surrounding bone.
codes.commonUse: Used when the root or surrounding bone must be seen, such as for pain, trauma, or endodontic assessment.
codes.distinctions: The first periapical at a visit is reported differently from each additional one. Count the images actually taken.
verifyQuestions: How many periapical images were taken at this visit?
Which tooth or area was imaged?

relationships.note: Each additional periapical at the same visit is reported separately.

codes.shortLabel: Intraoral periapical — each additional radiographic image
codes.plainLanguage: Each periapical image beyond the first taken at the same visit.
codes.commonUse: Reported alongside the first periapical when more than one is taken.
codes.distinctions: Reported per additional image. The number reported should match the number of images actually captured.
documentationConsiderations: Total number of periapical images taken
verifyQuestions: How many periapical images beyond the first were taken?

relationships.note: The first periapical at the visit is reported with its own code.

codes.plainLanguage: Two bitewing images, which show the crowns of upper and lower teeth in the same view.
codes.commonUse: Used to check for interproximal decay and bone levels, commonly at recall visits.
codes.distinctions: Bitewing codes are distinguished by the number of images taken. Two, three, four and vertical series are each reported differently.
verifyQuestions: How many bitewing images were taken?
Were they horizontal or vertical bitewings?

relationships.note: Four bitewing images are reported with a different code than two.

codes.plainLanguage: Four bitewing images, the most common bitewing set for an adult dentition.
codes.commonUse: The usual recall bitewing set where posterior teeth are present in all four quadrants.
codes.distinctions: Distinguished from the two-image and vertical bitewing codes purely by the number and type of images taken.
verifyQuestions: How many bitewing images were taken?
Were they horizontal or vertical bitewings?

relationships.note: Two bitewing images are reported with a different code than four.
Vertical bitewings of seven to eight images are reported separately.

codes.plainLanguage: Three bitewing images.
codes.commonUse: Used where three images cover the posterior contacts present, often in a mixed or reduced dentition.
codes.distinctions: Chosen by image count alone.
verifyQuestions: How many bitewing images were taken?

codes.shortLabel: Vertical bitewings — seven to eight radiographic images
codes.plainLanguage: A vertical bitewing series of seven or eight images, which shows more bone height than horizontal bitewings.
codes.commonUse: Often used where periodontal bone levels need to be assessed.
codes.distinctions: Distinguished from horizontal bitewings by orientation and image count. It is not a substitute for a complete series.
documentationConsiderations: That the images were vertical bitewings
Clinical reason, such as periodontal assessment
verifyQuestions: Were these vertical rather than horizontal bitewings?
How many images were taken?

codes.plainLanguage: A single extraoral image showing both arches and surrounding structures in one view.
codes.commonUse: Used for a broad survey, such as assessing third molars, pathology, or before surgical planning.
codes.distinctions: A panoramic image is not an intraoral complete series and does not show interproximal detail as well as bitewings.
documentationConsiderations: Clinical reason for the panoramic image
verifyQuestions: Why was a panoramic image indicated at this visit?

relationships.note: An intraoral complete series is a set of intraoral images rather than one extraoral image.

codes.plainLanguage: Removal of plaque, calculus and stain from the teeth, for a patient with an adult dentition.
codes.commonUse: The routine cleaning at a recall visit for an adult patient.
codes.distinctions: Separated from the child prophylaxis code by dentition rather than by a fixed birthday. It is also distinct from periodontal maintenance, which follows active periodontal therapy, and from scaling in the presence of inflammation.
documentationConsiderations: Periodontal status, which affects whether a prophylaxis or periodontal procedure applies
verifyQuestions: Is the patient's dentition permanent (adult) or primary/transitional (child)?
Has the patient had active periodontal therapy, which may make periodontal maintenance the appropriate service?

relationships.note: The child prophylaxis code applies to a primary or transitional dentition.
Periodontal maintenance follows active periodontal therapy and is a different service.
Scaling in the presence of generalised inflammation is a separate service from a routine prophylaxis.

codes.plainLanguage: Removal of plaque, calculus and stain for a patient with a primary or transitional dentition.
codes.commonUse: The routine cleaning at a recall visit for a child.
codes.distinctions: Chosen by dentition rather than age alone. A patient with a fully permanent dentition is generally reported with the adult code.
documentationConsiderations: That the dentition is primary or transitional
verifyQuestions: Is the patient's dentition primary or transitional rather than fully permanent?

relationships.note: The adult prophylaxis code applies to a permanent dentition.

codes.plainLanguage: Application of fluoride in varnish form to the teeth.
codes.commonUse: The usual fluoride application at a preventive visit, for children and for adults at elevated caries risk.
codes.distinctions: Separated from other topical fluoride forms (gel, foam, rinse) by the form applied. The note should say which was used.
documentationConsiderations: Caries risk or other reason for application
verifyQuestions: Was the fluoride applied as a varnish, or as a gel or foam?

relationships.note: Topical fluoride in a form other than varnish is reported separately.

codes.shortLabel: Topical application of fluoride — excluding varnish
codes.plainLanguage: Application of topical fluoride in a form other than varnish, such as a gel or foam.
codes.commonUse: Used where fluoride is delivered by tray or direct application rather than as a varnish.
codes.distinctions: The distinguishing fact is simply the form of fluoride used.
documentationConsiderations: Caries risk or other reason for application
verifyQuestions: Was the fluoride applied as a gel or foam rather than a varnish?

relationships.note: Fluoride varnish is reported with its own code.

codes.plainLanguage: A sealant placed in the pits and fissures of a tooth to prevent decay.
codes.commonUse: Most often placed on permanent molars shortly after eruption.
codes.distinctions: Reported per tooth, so the teeth sealed must be identified. A sealant is preventive: a tooth that already required a restoration is a different service.
documentationConsiderations: That the tooth surface was sound rather than restored
verifyQuestions: Which teeth were sealed?
Were the surfaces free of decay requiring restoration?

codes.shortLabel: Prefabricated stainless steel crown — primary tooth
codes.plainLanguage: A preformed stainless steel crown cemented over a primary tooth.
codes.commonUse: Commonly used on primary molars with extensive decay or after a pulpotomy.
codes.distinctions: Selected by dentition: there is a separate code for a permanent tooth. It is distinct from a laboratory-fabricated crown.
documentationConsiderations: That the crown was prefabricated stainless steel
verifyQuestions: Is the tooth primary or permanent?

relationships.note: The permanent-tooth version of this crown has its own code.

codes.shortLabel: Prefabricated stainless steel crown — permanent tooth
codes.plainLanguage: A preformed stainless steel crown cemented over a permanent tooth.
codes.commonUse: Used as an interim or definitive full-coverage restoration on a permanent tooth.
codes.distinctions: Selected by dentition: there is a separate code for a primary tooth.
documentationConsiderations: That the crown was prefabricated stainless steel
verifyQuestions: Is the tooth primary or permanent?

relationships.note: The primary-tooth version of this crown has its own code.

codes.plainLanguage: Re-cementing an existing crown that has come off, without making a new one.
codes.commonUse: Used when a crown de-bonds and is refitted intact.
codes.distinctions: Distinct from placing a new crown. If the crown is remade, a crown code applies instead.
documentationConsiderations: That the existing crown was refitted rather than replaced
Condition of the tooth and crown
verifyQuestions: Was the existing crown re-cemented, or was a new crown made?

codes.plainLanguage: Building up the remaining tooth structure so a crown has enough to hold onto.
codes.commonUse: Used when so little tooth structure remains that a crown could not be retained without it.
codes.distinctions: A buildup is for retention and structure, not simply to fill the space left by removing decay. If the material is placed only as a base or liner under a restoration, this is not the right code.
documentationConsiderations: That the buildup was needed for crown retention
verifyQuestions: Was the buildup necessary to retain the crown, rather than to fill out the preparation?
How much coronal tooth structure remained?

relationships.note: Where a post is placed in the root canal, the post and core code applies instead.

codes.shortLabel: Prefabricated post and core in addition to crown
codes.plainLanguage: A preformed post cemented into the root canal with a core built around it.
codes.commonUse: Used on an endodontically treated tooth where a post is needed to retain the core.
codes.distinctions: Distinct from a core buildup with no post, and from a cast post and core made in a laboratory.
documentationConsiderations: That the tooth has had root canal therapy
That a prefabricated post was placed
verifyQuestions: Was a post actually placed into the canal?
Was the post prefabricated or cast?

relationships.note: A cast post and core is fabricated rather than prefabricated.
A buildup with no post is reported differently.

codes.shortLabel: Cast post and core in addition to crown
codes.plainLanguage: A post and core cast as a single custom unit in a laboratory.
codes.commonUse: Used on an endodontically treated tooth where a custom cast post is chosen over a prefabricated one.
codes.distinctions: Distinguished from the prefabricated post and core by how the post was made.
documentationConsiderations: That the tooth has had root canal therapy
That the post and core was cast
verifyQuestions: Was the post and core cast in a laboratory rather than prefabricated?

relationships.note: A prefabricated post and core is not laboratory cast.

codes.plainLanguage: A temporary restoration placed to protect a tooth and relieve symptoms until definitive treatment.
codes.commonUse: Used as an interim measure, for example to settle symptoms before deciding on definitive treatment.
codes.distinctions: This is not a definitive filling. If a definitive restoration was placed at the same visit, that restoration is what is reported.
documentationConsiderations: That the restoration was protective or interim
verifyQuestions: Was this placed as an interim measure rather than a definitive restoration?

codes.plainLanguage: Placing medicament directly onto an exposed pulp to keep it vital.
codes.commonUse: Used when the pulp is exposed during caries removal or by trauma and is being preserved.
codes.distinctions: Direct capping requires an actual pulp exposure. Where the pulp is not exposed and a liner is placed over deep dentine, the indirect code applies.
verifyQuestions: Was the pulp actually exposed?

relationships.note: Indirect capping applies where the pulp was not exposed.

codes.plainLanguage: Placing medicament over a deep area of dentine close to the pulp, where the pulp itself is not exposed.
codes.commonUse: Used in deep caries where the pulp is approached but not exposed.
codes.distinctions: Distinguished from direct capping by whether the pulp was exposed.
documentationConsiderations: That the pulp was not exposed
verifyQuestions: Was the pulp exposed, or was it approached but left covered?

relationships.note: Direct capping applies where the pulp was exposed.

codes.shortLabel: Therapeutic pulpotomy — primary or permanent tooth
codes.plainLanguage: Removal of the coronal pulp, leaving the radicular pulp in place and treating it.
codes.commonUse: Commonly performed on primary molars, and sometimes as an interim measure on a permanent tooth.
codes.distinctions: A pulpotomy removes only the coronal pulp. Complete removal of the pulp through the canals is root canal therapy instead.
documentationConsiderations: That only the coronal pulp was removed
verifyQuestions: Was only the coronal pulp removed, or were the canals treated as well?

relationships.note: Full root canal therapy treats the canals rather than only the coronal pulp.

codes.plainLanguage: Root canal treatment of an anterior tooth, including cleaning, shaping and filling the canals.
codes.commonUse: Used where the pulp is irreversibly inflamed or necrotic and the tooth is being retained.
codes.distinctions: The root canal family is separated by tooth position — anterior, premolar, or molar. The tooth number determines which applies, so it is essential.
documentationConsiderations: That the canals were treated and obturated
verifyQuestions: Which tooth was treated?
Were all canals cleaned, shaped and filled at this visit?

relationships.note: Same procedure on a tooth in a different position class.
Same procedure on a tooth in a different position class.

codes.shortLabel: Scaling and root planing — four or more teeth per quadrant
codes.plainLanguage: Cleaning of the root surfaces below the gum line in a quadrant with four or more affected teeth.
codes.commonUse: Used to treat periodontitis where there is attachment loss and calculus on the root surfaces.
codes.distinctions: Separated from the one-to-three-teeth code by how many teeth in the quadrant were treated. It is also distinct from a routine prophylaxis and from scaling for gingival inflammation.
documentationConsiderations: How many teeth in that quadrant were treated
verifyQuestions: Which quadrant was treated?
How many teeth in that quadrant were scaled and root planed?
Is there periodontal charting supporting the diagnosis?

relationships.note: One to three teeth in a quadrant is reported with a different code.
A routine prophylaxis is a preventive cleaning, not periodontal therapy.
Scaling for generalised gingival inflammation applies where there is no attachment loss.

codes.shortLabel: Scaling and root planing — one to three teeth per quadrant
codes.plainLanguage: Cleaning of the root surfaces below the gum line in a quadrant where one to three teeth are affected.
codes.commonUse: Used for localised periodontal involvement within a quadrant.
codes.distinctions: Separated from the four-or-more code by the number of teeth treated in that quadrant.
documentationConsiderations: How many teeth in that quadrant were treated
verifyQuestions: Which quadrant was treated?
How many teeth in that quadrant were scaled and root planed?

relationships.note: Four or more teeth in a quadrant is reported with a different code.

codes.shortLabel: Scaling in the presence of generalised moderate or severe gingival inflammation — full mouth
codes.plainLanguage: A full-mouth scaling for a patient with widespread gingival inflammation but without attachment loss.
codes.commonUse: Used where inflammation is generalised and a routine prophylaxis would not address it, but periodontitis is not present.
codes.distinctions: Distinguished from scaling and root planing by the absence of attachment loss, and from a prophylaxis by the extent of inflammation.
documentationConsiderations: That there is no attachment loss (which would indicate periodontal therapy)
verifyQuestions: Is there generalised inflammation without attachment loss?
Does the charting show pocketing and attachment loss?

relationships.note: Scaling and root planing applies where there is attachment loss.
A routine prophylaxis applies where inflammation is not generalised.

codes.shortLabel: Full mouth debridement to enable comprehensive evaluation and diagnosis
codes.plainLanguage: Removal of heavy deposits that prevent a proper examination from being carried out.
codes.commonUse: Used at a first visit where deposits are so heavy that the dentition cannot be evaluated.
codes.distinctions: This enables an evaluation rather than being a definitive cleaning. A comprehensive evaluation normally follows at a later visit.
documentationConsiderations: That a comprehensive evaluation could not be completed at the same visit
verifyQuestions: Did the deposits genuinely prevent examination and diagnosis?
Was a comprehensive evaluation deferred to a later visit?

codes.plainLanguage: Ongoing periodontal care following active periodontal therapy, including removal of deposits above and below the gum line.
codes.commonUse: Used at recall visits for a patient who has completed periodontal treatment.
codes.distinctions: Applies after active periodontal therapy. A patient who has never had periodontal therapy generally receives a prophylaxis instead.
documentationConsiderations: Date of the previous periodontal treatment
verifyQuestions: Has the patient completed active periodontal therapy?
